# Native Muscle Contact Replay

## Scope and Evidence

F07b (#11815, parent #11791) extends `replay_muscle_excitations` with an
explicit `contact_force_paths` tuple. Default replay remains muscle and gravity
only. Each listed absolute native component path must identify a registered
`HuntCrossleyForce` or `SmoothSphereHalfSpaceForce`; arbitrary external forces,
reserves, existing controllers and prescribed motion remain forbidden.

The OpenSim model owns the contact calculation. The replay neither adds
external contact inputs nor substitutes a shared rigid-body law. Complete named
continuous initialization, the single cold-start Runge-Kutta-Merson integrator
and time-only bounded excitation playback follow the native replay chapter.

## Wrench Extraction and Identity

The existing `OpenSimForceTorqueSource` reads native record values and transforms
forces, moments and application points into its world Z-up frame. Returned
`contact_wrenches` are immutable tuples of frozen wrench records, one tuple per
output time. Each listed force must produce exactly one supported sphere/half-space
wrench on the sphere body; the plane must be fixed to ground and the sphere
must belong to a moving body. HuntCrossley parameters must reference exactly
that pair, without additional silently omitted geometry. Body-to-body contact
needs a separate policy with both affected bodies' evidence. Omitted geometry,
ambiguous names, missing torque or nonfinite values
cause failure; they do not become zero contact evidence.

Policy version `native-muscle-replay/1.1.0` records the sorted path allowlist,
native force class, contact frame, integrator accuracy and all prior drive
policies. Model-byte identity covers material, friction, dissipation, smoothing,
geometry and socket settings serialized in the model. Referenced resources and
plugin/discrete state completeness still require separate qualification.

## Synthetic Native Validation

The regression model contains one compliant Millard muscle, a slider load and
native smooth or HuntCrossley sphere/half-space contact opposing muscle contraction. Tests check
positive native reaction direction, complete wrench evidence, deterministic
repeat integration, a different trajectory when contact is removed, and state
agreement within `2e-5` for integrator accuracy `1e-6` versus `1e-9` over `0.08 s`.
These are fixture-specific numerical checks, not physiological acceptance limits.

The fixture allows bounded compliant indentation. Smooth contact can exert
small forces outside geometric contact because of its native smoothing law;
full-body acceptance must quantify that leakage against a declared budget.
The synthetic smooth fixture explicitly uses `constant_contact_force=1e-12`,
`hertz_smoothing=5e4`, `hunt_crossley_smoothing=50`, `stiffness=1e7` and
`dissipation=1`; native force at initial touch and gaps of `10`, `20`, `100`
and `1000` micrometres is required below the fixture-specific `0.01 N` budget.
The native smooth law's force at touch is about `0.000236 N`, but the
`20` micrometre gap gives about `0.00504 N`; the gap sweep matters because
leakage is nonmonotone.
With the default regularizer `1e-5`, the same fixture produced about `41.9 N`
at touch. Changing only smoothing slopes did not remove that bias. These
failed trials are retained here to prevent treating native defaults as
validated material parameters.
The regularizer also affects near-zero-slip friction and native reported
potential energy is an approximation across smoothing. Future friction and
energy acceptance must check the executed law and integrated force/work;
this zero-slip fixture does not qualify those properties.
Strict zero force outside contact or rigid zero penetration cannot qualify a
compliant law. Neither matching a force class name nor passing these tests
establishes native HuntCrossley/smooth/shared-law parity.

## Remaining Qualification

Full-body muscle paths, region and wrist coverage, force/length/moment-arm
validation, model-owned ground and grip mechanics, contact calibration and
full-horizon private mocap matching remain open. Recorded diagnostic wrenches
are outputs, never additional injected contact forces. Replay results do not
constitute a scientific acceptance certificate.
